title: Validation Technical Reference
readerIntent: Audit validation placement, extension, status handling, and test completeness.
owner: Owning capabilities plus shared validation, policy, pipeline, and status contracts
summary: A complete rule identifies its authority, execution boundary, configuration, stable failure contract, observability, and cross-entry-path evidence.

sections.heading: Validation layers
items: Transport validation checks shape and limits; schema validation checks types and constraints; authorization checks principal policy; services enforce business invariants and transitions.
Provider adapters validate technology-specific capability and mapping behind provider-neutral contracts. Frontend validation improves feedback but never replaces backend enforcement.
Each rule has one authority and all create, update, import, workflow, event, assistant, and scheduled entry paths reach it.

sections.heading: Declarative and behavioral placement
items: Place stable field type, required, range, format, default, immutability, and relationship constraints in schema declarations.
Place cross-record, state-transition, external evidence, concurrency, and context-dependent rules in owning services or supported interceptors.
Keep reusable policy names and thresholds in properties.js so customer layers can extend them without editing schema closures.

sections.heading: Errors and security
items: Return stable registered codes and field-safe messages while preserving causal details in protected diagnostics with correlation.
Do not reveal masked fields, credentials, existence of unauthorized records, internal paths, stacks, queries, or provider payloads.
Normalize and reject unknown fields, prototype-sensitive paths, unsupported operators, oversized collections, and ambiguous related references.

sections.heading: Verification and evolution
items: Test valid, invalid, missing, empty, minimum, maximum, malformed, malicious, duplicate, concurrent, cross-tenant, ownership, and field-mask cases.
Exercise every entry path plus import/export, publishing, search, cache, workflow, events, scheduled jobs, assistant tools, migration, and legacy records.
A changed rule includes compatibility, data assessment, migration, rollback, layered customization, documentation, and regression evidence.

sections.heading: Implementation checklist
items: Rule and capability owner are explicit.
Declarative versus behavioral placement is justified.
All mutation and query entry paths reach the authority.
Tenant, enterprise, ownership, group, field, and principal-type policy is preserved.
Configuration is layered and extensible rather than hidden in schema closures or controller constants.
Stable success and error codes are registered and validated.
Sensitive values are masked in responses, logs, metrics, and audit.
Positive, negative, boundary, contract, integration, security, and regression tests exist.

sections.heading: Extension rules
items: A customer module may add stricter policy through an existing layered validator or interceptor.
It must not weaken framework security silently or bypass the owning capability.
Frontend validation is an experience enhancement, never backend authority.
Provider-specific validation remains behind the provider-neutral contract.
A new governance layer requires a duplication and parallel-path audit first.
